newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures post huge losses, finish lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures post huge losses, finish lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures posted huge losses in heavy trading after Alan Greenspan's testimony struck rate-hike fear in the hearts of bulls.

The Federal Reserve chief, in the first leg of his semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, told the Senate Banking Committee the U.S. stock market's rise may be "unsustainable." And he said the Fed may need to raise rates before inflation gets worse.
"I think that people are finally capitulating and believing that Greenspan wants to do something," said John Nyhoff, chief economist with Mitsubishi Financial Futures.
Nyhoff said slipping through support at 94.08 in September Eurodollars and 94.24 in June helped fuel the fire.
He said players may be speculating about just how much of a proactive stance Greenspan will take.
"The longer they wait the larger the probablility that maybe we'll be (tightening) 50 basis points," Nyhoff said.

The original post-Greenspan push lower took March to 111-7/32, where a flurry of retail buying stemmed losses and took March back to a support band from 111-25/32 to 27/32. That zone is a cluster of old weekly highs from December that some had thought would be a new bottom for the market.
But after a sloppy five-year note auction, March revisited the session lows and handily erased support at 111-3/32 to 5/32 and at 111-00 before slipping as low as 110-25/32.
Treasury sold $12.5 billion notes at a 6.359 percent yield, with 37 percent of the bids awarded at the high.
The bid-to-cover ratio was 2.11, with non-competitive bids at $499 million.
The huge losses came on the heels of an extremely quiet first hour of trade that saw trading halted due to a technical glitch at the Chicago Board of Trade.
Trade re-opened before Greenspan's testimony began.

If preliminary estimates hold true, the day's T-bond futures volume will be the third largest ever, according to Chicago Board of Trade estimates. The CBOT said 735,000 contracts traded Wednesday, compared with 418,260 on Tuesday.

"It was a break on aggressive selling," said Donald Pullen, ED and F Man's bond trading floor manager. "I think this means there's a bearish tone coming into the market into the end of the week," he said.
He said Greenspan comments started the ball rolling, with technical selling flaring up on the breakdown under 112-00 and 111-16/32.

At the end of pit trading, March T-bonds were down 1-23/32 points to 110-28/32, 10-year notes lost 1-4/32 to 108-12/32, munis fell 1-10/32 to 115-25/32, June T-bills fell 12 bps at 94.80, and June Eurodollars fell 12 bps at 94.25. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
